output.question: Find the top trending Python and Rust repos this week and this month, rank by momentum, and keep only what's relevant to agentic / MCP / dev-tooling with a one-line why-it-matters each.
output.findings:
The current trend in developer tooling is heavily focused on 'agentic' workflows, with Python dominating the orchestration layer and Rust powering high-performance infrastructure and CLI utilities. Key repositories include 'claude-code' (agentic coding), 'headroom' (token optimization), and 'dograh' (voice AI platform), all of which are actively integrating with the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Top Python picks include 'microsoft/markitdown' (document-to-markdown conversion for LLMs), 'anthropics/claude-code' (agentic terminal coding), and 'dograh-hq/dograh' (MCP-native voice AI). These tools are critical for building robust, context-aware AI agents that can interact with real-world data and systems.

Top Rust picks include 'farion1231/cc-switch' (all-in-one assistant for various coding agents), 'run-llama/liteparse' (high-performance document parsing), and 'ogulcancelik/herdr' (agent multiplexer). These projects demonstrate the shift toward using Rust for low-latency, resource-efficient AI infrastructure that complements Python-based agent logic.
